steps.note: The plan traces rows 0-7 (subtract Ja+Rc, change scratch to a+Vx, c+Gx, add back, restore) and concludes the net change (JV+RG)x is independent of a,c, quoting line 748.

The plan states the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, that side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one pairs, that intersections 0 and 2 already give 0, and that the self coefficient is 1.
The plan never treats the complex case: neither the central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 nor the side wires cancelling intersections zero and two appears anywhere.
The plan gives the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), with the inverse middle stage and each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.
S1.1.3.3 asserts that every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels but gives none of the per-edge orthogonal residuals or their dimensions from the residual table.

S1.1.3.2 states that t_X perp t_Y allows P(x)<t_X> inside P(x)t_Y^perp (quoting the gate-label passage at line 953), but it never gives the side edge 2->5 residual <t_X,t_Y>^perp or its dimension h-2.
The plan states that the only decreasing edge is center 3->4 with loss h, and that telescoping gives sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N and absolute Wm-2N+2L.
The plan uses an orthonormal basis of each residual (S2.1, S2.1.1) but never argues over F2 that nonzero residuals are nondegenerate and nonalternating, nor that alternating planes are absorbed.
The plan states that orthogonal binary supports meet evenly, so weight is additive mod 4, giving q_V-q_U as the sum of wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal basis of the residual.

S2.1.1 jumps from odd weight straight to the kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse; it never states the phase i^{eps[v.x]} or the conversion H diag(1,-1) H = X that turns the character into a translation, so it asserts the result without the step.
The plan states that each residual basis vector gives exactly one forward factor C^{(x)f} on the f axes (columns) of a slot, and that summing residual dimensions gives s_c such factors.

S2.1.5 and the S2.1 method name the endpoint Z signs, the scalar i^{27f}, C=iZC^{-1}Z and the X-output negation, but they omit the frames I and C^{(x)m} for the zero and full labels and the C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) that the repair corrects.
The plan states L_b/N<1/2 and that s_b falls short of W_b m by N-2L_b>0.
S1.1.4 gives the relative deficit (W_b m-s_b)/(W_b m)=339/22587335000000.
The plan gives the complex deficit 2N-2L_c>0 (S2.1.2) but never the relative deficit eta_c=73/19906842167500.
S1.1.4 states that the deficit exceeds 20*2^{-50}, that log m<20 gives m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50}), and so s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}; S5.1.1 sets sigma=tau.

S1.1.5.1 states the factorization with lower-triangular E1,E2 and a partial permutation with exactly a ones, found by elimination with the rightmost entry of the topmost nonzero row as pivot; repeating on the active indices is left implicit.

S1.1.5 mentions only in passing 'q a fixed prime avoiding all denominators'; it never ties the prime to the finite table of factors and inverses, nor says that the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.
S1.1.5.2 states the O(V) lower-triangular transformation, updating coordinates in descending physical order from earlier coordinates that still hold their original values.
S1.1.5.3 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, the interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j, yielding (h+d,d) with one interchange, so there are a recursive calls in all.
The plan mentions C_0 d^{C_1}, C_1=20 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) (S2.5, S5.1.1) but never defines E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3} or C_0=128mB^2.
No step gives the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with leaf bound 8e or the per-invocation operation count; S2.5 only asserts the depth bound C_0 d^{C_1}.
The unrolling B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu, A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} and the total below C_0 d^{C_1} are absent; S2.5 states only the final bound.
S2.5 states that a value at depth j lies in 2^{-(p+j)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^j, and that p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact with Delta=o(p); S5.1.1 gives epsilon C_1<1.
S2.6 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and the single truncation errs by less than sqrt2 2^{-p}.

summary: P08 is 15 of 26. It covers in detail the scalar bit motif (B1, B2, B4), the label telescoping and loss ratios (L3, L5), the bit rank saving (R1, R2, R4), the matrix shear (M1, M3, M4) and the layer's guard-bit and disk arguments (S4, S5). It omits the complex motif case (B3), the residual table, the side-edge h-2 residual and the F2 orthonormal-basis argument (L1, L2, L4), the phase-to-kernel conversion and endpoint repair details (P2, P4), eta_c (R3), the prime-specialization step (M2), and the whole arithmetic-depth derivation (S1-S3).
